newsitem.title: MALAWI: MALAWI EARMARKS $40 MILLION TO REHABILITATE POWER.
newsitem.headline: MALAWI EARMARKS $40 MILLION TO REHABILITATE POWER.

text.p: Malawi is to spend more than $40 million in a two-year programme to rehabilitate its power supply system which is in virtual collapse, officials said on Wednesday.

Raynold Duncan, the head of the country's sole power supplier, Electricity Supply Commission (ESCOM), told Reuters equipment supplying power to the country was too old to distribute electricity effectively.
"Most of the problems experienced are due to a very weak distribution system," Duncan said.
"The problem is that we don't have money," he added.
Power cuts are a daily occurance in Malawi, sometimes arising from technical faults and in other cases from official load-shedding to preserve the worn-out machinery.
Duncan said the parastatal had launched several programmes to install sub-stations in the country's main industrial cities of Blantyre and Lilongwe.
He said projects were also being implemented to remove a buildup of silt and sand from the Shire river which had helped to cripple the main generators.
ESCOM is presently scouting for funding of 100 million kwacha ($6.7 million) from local banks to begin some of the programmes.
Foreign funding for the remaining $33.3 million will be 70 percent for soft loans to the government and 30 percent commercial credit to be received from Sweden, Japan and Spain.
ESCOM, which supplies power to only four percent of the country's 12-million population, has been operating on a 25 million kwacha ($1.7 million) overdraft over the past two years, Duncan said.
"What should be known is that ESCOM does not get any subvention (subsidy) from government. It's a commercial parastatal," he said.
